# Introduction to Natural Language Processing

:::{.hero-lead}
From linguistic foundations to modern language models, with rigorous lectures, practical notebooks, and research-driven projects.
:::

:::{.course-meta}
`14 weeks`{.meta-pill} `Lectures & notes`{.meta-pill} `Coding projects`{.meta-pill} `Project presentations`{.meta-pill}
:::
:::

:::{.hero-visual}
![A visual journey from multilingual language and speech through tokens, embeddings, attention networks, and NLP applications](./images/nlp-hero-2026.png){.nlp-demo}
:::

:::

:::{.description-text}
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to Natural Language Processing (NLP), covering theoretical foundations and practical applications. Through lectures, detailed coding sessions, and independent research projects, students will learn to build systems that analyze, understand, and generate human language.
:::

## Reference Books

:::{.book-container}

:::{.book-card}
![Cover of Speech and Language Processing, third edition](./images/slp3-cover.jpg){.book-image}

**Speech and Language Processing**  
*Daniel Jurafsky & James H. Martin*

Our core reference: a rigorous bridge from words and n-grams to transformers, LLM post-training, RAG, translation, and speech. Updated January 2026.

[📖 Read the 3rd Edition](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/)
:::

:::{.book-card}
![Cover of Natural Language Processing with Transformers](./images/nlp-transformers-cover.webp){.book-image}

**Natural Language Processing with Transformers**  
*Lewis Tunstall, Leandro von Werra & Thomas Wolf*

A practical companion for building, fine-tuning, evaluating, and optimizing transformer applications with the Hugging Face ecosystem.

[📖 View at O'Reilly](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/natural-language-processing/9781098136789/)
:::

:::
